newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Seven offers received for Lithuania Telecom tender.
newsitem.headline: Seven offers received for Lithuania Telecom tender.

text.p: Lithuania's European affairs ministry said on Thursday it had received seven bids to become lead advisor to the government on the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom.

Alfredas Ramanauskas, deputy director of the ministry's privatisation department, told Reuters that the ministry received offers from Creditanstalt Invesment Bank, Union Bank of Switzerland, Banque Paribas and Clifford Chance, Flemings and Hansa Investments, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell with Nomura International.
The tender deadline expired on Wednesday.
The other bidders were N.M. Rothschild & Sons Ltd and Squire, Sanders and Dempsey and Daiwa Institute of Research.
"Today the tender commission will start consideration of the offers and we expect it will last no later than the middle of next week," Ramanauskas said.
"In case there are some equally good offers the commission might ask for additional presentation from the participants," Ramanauskas added.
The 100 percent state-run telephone company is one of 13 key enterprises slated for sale by Lithuania's right-of-centre government, which has vowed to speed the pace of privatisation.
The government said earlier it expected to start the actual privatisation of the firm early in 1998.
